name: Spinal Cord Arteriovenous Malformation

criteria.description: Visualization of abnormal arteriovenous shunting within the spinal cord on spinal angiography or MRI/MRA
Presence of progressive myelopathy symptoms such as motor weakness, sensory disturbances, or sphincter dysfunction
Exclusion of other causes of spinal cord vascular lesions or compressive myelopathy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Definitive diagnosis requires imaging confirmation of spinal AVM combined with compatible clinical symptoms and exclusion of alternative diagnoses.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Spinal angiography remains the gold standard for diagnosis.

laboratory: No specific laboratory abnormalities; routine blood tests typically normal
imaging: MRI showing flow voids, spinal cord edema, or hemorrhage
genetic: No known genetic mutations directly associated; mostly sporadic cases
other: Electrophysiological studies may show conduction abnormalities
Neurological examination revealing upper motor neuron signs

distinguishingFeatures: Mass lesion on MRI without vascular flow voids
Progressive symptoms without acute hemorrhagic episodes
MRI showing cord swelling without abnormal vascular structures
Sudden onset with vascular risk factors
MRI showing ischemic changes without AV shunting

redFlags: Sudden onset of severe neurological deficit
Rapid progression of motor weakness and sensory loss
Signs of spinal cord hemorrhage or acute myelopathy
